# Digest: Minovitch 1972, "Gravity Thrust Jupiter Orbiter Trajectories Generated by Encountering the Galilean Satellites" (#960 batch 28; #943)

M. A. Minovitch (JPL), Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets 9(10):751-756 (October 1972), doi
10.2514/3.30391.
- Filed as `cyclers_pdf/papers/minovitch-1972-gravity-thrust-jupiter-orbiter-trajectories-galilean-satellites-jsr-9-10-751-doi-10.2514-3.30391.pdf`.
  6 pp., text layer, md5 df1cb2f330ec294163cba337a7b6ebce. Supplied by the owner.
- I read the whole paper. Table 1 was read on the page image (p.754).

## 0. Verdict (sent to twobody-gen2-opus)

**No collision with `#943` gc or ge.**
- Table 1 is one non-periodic 19-encounter tour, Dec 1979 to Sep 1980 (263.7 d), with the sequence
  E C E G I E G I E G C I E G I E G I E.
- The v_inf values are high: Ganymede 12.25-12.65 km/s, Callisto 8.13-8.52, Europa 15.3-16.8, Io
  17.9-21.0.
- There are multi-revolution legs (0-2 revolutions), and the period falls from 14.2 to 7.9 d (Fig. 1).
  The sum of the gravitational dV is 3.595 km/s.
- **Periodic tours:** the paper defines "periodic GT trajectories" (m1-...-mn repeating) and cites only
  Hollister's Earth-Venus and Earth-Mars periodic orbits (Hollister & Menning 1970, Hollister & Rall
  1971, both held). It states that "chances of finding periodic GT trajectories involving all four
  Galilean satellites ... appear to be rather remote". No two-moon periodic sequence is given.
- **Early prior art:** this is the 1972 statement of a periodic multi-moon tour as a goal. It is
  citable history for the moon-cycler literature (before Russell & Strange 2009).

## 1. Content (READ)

- **Existence theorem** (proof in Appendix A): with multiple revolutions between encounters allowed,
  small-satellite perturbations can be magnified so that any satellite of the sequence can eventually be
  reached.
- The tour without multi-revolution legs fails after the 6th encounter (negative closest approach),
  because the capture orbit is too eccentric.
- Circular coplanar satellite orbits with true inclinations are used. With the JPL ephemeris, T3 shifts
  0.785 hr and the closest approaches change (7,322.7 to 40,441.2 km at m2).
- Mission context: Earth-Jupiter launch 26.12 Aug 1977, C3 99.8 km^2/s^2, 766 d flight, orbit insertion
  dV 1.215 km/s, 934 kg, Titan 3D(7)/Centaur.
- Table 2: five Lambert orbits for fixed conditions.

## 2. Citation mining

- Minovitch TR 32-464 [5] is cited as "TR 32-464, Oct. 31, 1963", with no NTRS or N-number. That makes
  four sources for 32-464 against Niehoff's 32-468.
- Held: Minovitch TM 312-130 (1961) [2], in the documents gallery part 1; Hollister & Menning 1970 [8];
  Hollister & Rall 1971 [9].
- Niehoff 1971, "Touring the Galilean Satellites", JSR 8(10):1021 [1]: the journal form of the held
  AIAA 70-1070. It is added to the wanted list for attribution.
- Not held, not added: Minovitch 1968 (AAS Sci. Tech. Ser. 17, "Gravity thrust and interplanetary
  transportation networks") [3]; JPL internal report 393-72 [4]; TR 32-1529 [6]; JPL IOM 93.1-231 [7].
